# STEP importer: source, rebuild and relink instructions

This download accompanies Wire EDM Workbench's unmodified `occt-import-js`
0.0.23 JavaScript/WebAssembly library. It is a developer source distribution;
using STEP import in the hosted app requires none of these build tools.

Download **both** source archives and `occt-import-js-sources.json` from this same
directory. The importer archive contains its complete source, CMake project,
Windows build scripts, examples and tests. Its `occt/` Git submodule is not
embedded: the separate OCCT archive supplies that directory, including OCCT's
source, build files and license notices. Neither archive has been repacked or
modified by Wire EDM Workbench.

| Archive | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `occt-import-js-c2148e54b456b571238d35cac037d304053d64b2.tar.gz` | 4399573 | `2bd3799b2ac56cbf3f0df6300a51c8890e137bd001462702b356f621e33ff192` |
| `OCCT-d2abb6d844231cb8f29be6894440874a4700e4a5.tar.gz` | 48218968 | `2715d89a1bc44dfd34dab88f729c445ea93f6b57d6539b0c89614a80ae144a6c` |

The importer commit is the npm release's recorded `gitHead`. Its Git tree pins
the OCCT submodule to the second revision. That OCCT tree has no further Git
submodules. Provenance:

- [Importer source tree](https://github.com/kovacsv/occt-import-js/tree/c2148e54b456b571238d35cac037d304053d64b2)
- [OCCT source tree](https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/tree/d2abb6d844231cb8f29be6894440874a4700e4a5)
- [npm release metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/occt-import-js/0.0.23)

## Restore the source layout

On Windows, place the two verified downloads in an empty working directory.
PowerShell's `Get-FileHash` can verify the SHA-256 values above. Windows `tar`
can restore the layout without fetching a Git submodule:

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\*.tar.gz -Algorithm SHA256
tar -xzf .\occt-import-js-c2148e54b456b571238d35cac037d304053d64b2.tar.gz
Set-Location .\occt-import-js-c2148e54b456b571238d35cac037d304053d64b2
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force .\occt
tar -xzf ..\OCCT-d2abb6d844231cb8f29be6894440874a4700e4a5.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C .\occt
```

The resulting tree must contain `CMakeLists.txt`, `occt-import-js/src/`,
`tools/`, and `occt/src/`. Retain the importer `LICENSE.md`, OCCT
`LICENSE_LGPL_21.txt`, `OCCT_LGPL_EXCEPTION.txt`, and the notices in individual
source files.

## Rebuild the library

The pinned upstream WASM workflow uses Windows 2022, Node 18 for its JavaScript
tests, CMake, and the included batch scripts. Install Git and CMake and make
them available in the build shell. The CMake project declares a minimum of
3.6; use a current compatible CMake installation for its complete feature set.

From the restored importer root, the upstream sequence is:

```powershell
.\tools\setup_emscripten_win.bat
.\tools\build_wasm_win_release.bat
npm install
npm test
```

Check each command's exit status before continuing. The setup script downloads
the Emscripten SDK and selects **Emscripten 3.1.69** and **MinGW 7.1.0 64-bit**.
These are developer build tools; no SDK is downloaded during STEP import in the
app. The upstream scripts and CMake options are supplied unchanged in the
importer archive. The upstream tests load the new files from
`build/wasm/Release/`. The resulting library files are:

- `build/wasm/Release/occt-import-js.js`
- `build/wasm/Release/occt-import-js.wasm`

The original source archive's WASM is byte-identical to the npm WASM. Its loader
uses LF endings; the npm loader differs only by CRLF endings on its 19 lines.
The accompanying manifest records the exact npm artifact hashes used by this
Workbench release. The source/build instructions have been inspected; a full
library recompilation and bit-for-bit reproducibility of a new build have not
been established here. Toolchain differences can affect generated bytes.

## Modify and relink with Wire EDM Workbench

The [Workbench source repository](https://github.com/Insignifi4nt/wireedm-gcode-parser)
provides its package lock, worker integration and build configuration. Use the
source tag matching the app version shown in Settings. The worker imports the
loader from `occt-import-js` and the WASM from
`occt-import-js/dist/occt-import-js.wasm`; both are bundled into the app.

After building a modified library, copy its generated loader and WASM over the
matching two files in the Workbench checkout's
`node_modules/occt-import-js/dist/`. Keep those two files from the same build.
Running the Workbench development build then uses the replacement library;
reinstalling dependencies will restore the original npm files.

The production source-distribution check intentionally rejects unrecorded
binary changes. For redistribution of a modified library, update its recorded
binary hashes and include your patches or complete modified source, together
with any changed build instructions, in the corresponding source downloads.
Update `scripts/distribute-step-sources.ts` and its manifest to package and
verify that source. Preserve the original notices and clearly identify the
modifications. The integration source and build scripts can themselves be
modified; there is no separate proprietary relinking step.

Local copies of the LGPL 2.1 texts and Open CASCADE exception accompany these
downloads. This record documents the distributed artifacts and build process;
it is not a legal certification.
